title: Interior and Glasshouse
premise: Emrys Pemberton, once a celebrated composition prodigy, returns to the conservatory where her mother taught, now working as a janitor and hiding behind a borrowed name. When a student performs a melody Emrys wrote as a child—a piece never recorded, never published—she realizes someone has been passing her mother's private notebooks through the school for years. Tracing the song's journey forces Emrys to confront the estranged friend who took credit for her early work and to finally grieve the mother she left without a goodbye. The novel ends with Emrys performing the unfinished duet they wrote together at the conservatory's winter recital, signing it with both their names, and choosing to stay—not as a tenant, but as a teacher.
about_author: W. M. Coldharbour is the pen name of a former conservatory caretaker who spent a decade sweeping practice rooms before publishing short fiction in small literary journals. Interior and Glasshouse is their first novel, written largely in the margins of maintenance logs.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Emrys: she mops the conservatory's glasshouse corridor at dawn, invisible among students who never look up. Flashbacks establish her childhood here as a prodigy and her mother's death three years ago, unattended. Emotional beat: the numb safety of anonymity, and its first hairline crack when a student calls her 'ma'am' and sees her.

chapters.title: A Song With No Address
chapters.summary: Emrys hears a first-year violinist practicing 'Lullaby for the North Window'—a piece nine-year-old Emrys wrote with her mother and never showed anyone. She confronts the girl gently; the student says it came from a photocopied folder passed down through generations of students. Beat: vertigo—the past is circulating without her permission.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Emrys breaks into the conservatory's locked archive after hours and finds her mother's donated notebooks, catalogued under another name: Halvard Reyes, her childhood duet partner and closest friend. POV shifts briefly to Halvard via an inserted letter. Beat: betrayal surfaces—her grief curdles into accusation before she can read the whole record.

chapters.title: What Halvard Kept
chapters.summary: Emrys tracks down Halvard, now a mid-list composer in the city. He reveals he didn't steal the songs; her mother gave him the notebooks before dying, asking him to keep the music alive because Emrys had disappeared. Beat: the ground shifts—her invisibility was a wound she inflicted on everyone, not just herself.

chapters.title: Glasshouse Weather
chapters.summary: Back at work, Emrys begins secretly restoring damaged pages of the notebooks during night shifts, reading her mother's marginalia for the first time—including notes addressed to adult Emrys, whom her mother predicted would come back angry. The head custodian notices and says nothing. Beat: tenderness breaking through guilt.

chapters.title: The Student Who Plays Like Her
chapters.summary: The violinist, Noor, asks the janitor's opinion on interpretation, having noticed how she mouths the phrasing. Their unlikely friendship grows over shared practice-room hours; Noor is a scholarship kid terrified of being a fraud. Beat: found family begins forming in the mirror of teacher and student.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Halvard announces a retrospective concert featuring 'the Reyes juvenilia,' and the conservatory plans to honor him. Emrys must decide whether to expose the truth or let her mother's gift stand mislabeled forever. Rising tension: she drafts an email to the director, deletes it, drafts again. Beat: justice versus protection—neither feels clean.

chapters.title: North Window
chapters.summary: Climax approaches: Emrys finds the final notebook page—an unfinished duet titled 'Interior and Glasshouse,' with her mother's instruction: 'finish it with her.' A confrontation with Halvard turns raw; he admits he was waiting for her to claim it, even hoping she'd hate him enough to return. Beat: grief and anger fuse into resolve.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: At the winter recital, before Halvard is honored, Emrys walks onstage uninvited, tells the room whose hands actually wrote the juvenilia, and plays the completed duet—her part and the ghost of her mother's, with Noor joining on violin. Beat: catharsis; saying goodbye properly, publicly, out loud.

chapters.title: Owner
chapters.summary: Resolution: the conservatory offers Emrys a teaching post in composition; she hangs her name beside her mother's on the studio door. Halvard and she begin repairing what remains repairable. Final image: dawn in the glasshouse, mop retired, morning light through glass like a held breath released. Beat: belonging, chosen at last.
